sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head pale brown, slightly paler posteriorly, clypeus yellowish brown, mandibles blackish brown, antennae, pronotum and legs pale yellow, abdomen yellowish white; head and thorax sparsely hairy. Head nearly rectangular, the lateral margins weakly convex, the posterior margin nearly rounded, the anterolateral corners not projecting; fontanelle very small, slightly above the middle of the head; antenna 13-segmented, segment 2 more than twice as long as segment 3, segment 3 the shortest and narrowest, the segments lengthening from segment 5 on; postclypeus strongly sclerotized, distinctly wider than long; labrum nearly rectangular, wider than long; mandibles sickle-shaped, slender and elongate, incurved at the apex, the inner margin slightly coarsely serrate, with a distinct tooth slightly below the middle of each mandible; postmentum club-shaped, widest at the anterior third, narrowest below the posterior third. Alate not described. Compared with M. heimi, M. tenuignathus and M. insularis: the mandibles are slender, gradually incurved and slightly coarsely serrate (in the latter three the mandibles are thick, nearly straight and abruptly bent at the apex), and the postmentum and the waist are more strongly narrowed.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale brown, slightly paler posteriorly; labrum yellowish brown; mandibles blackish brown; antennae, pronotum and legs pale yellow; abdomen yellowish white. Head and thorax sparsely hairy. Head nearly rectangular, the lateral margins weakly convex, the posterior margin nearly rounded, the anterolateral corners not projecting; frons distinctly inclined forward, the Y-shaped suture indistinct; fontanelle very small, slightly above the middle of the head. Antenna 13-segmented, segment 2 more than twice as long as segment 3 and slightly longer than segment 4, segment 3 the shortest and narrowest, the segments lengthening from segment 5 on. Postclypeus strongly sclerotized, distinctly wider than long, with a few short and long hairs; anteclypeus white, more than twice as long as wide, hairless. Labrum nearly rectangular, wider than long, the anterior margin nearly rounded, the anterior half with several erect hairs. Mandibles sickle-shaped, slender and elongate, rather distinctly incurved at the apex, the inner margin slightly coarsely serrate, with a distinct tooth slightly below the middle of each mandible. Postmentum club-shaped, widest at the anterior third, narrowest below the posterior third, the narrowest width slightly less than the widest width, the widest width about half its median length; anterior margin nearly straight, with a few short hairs, posterior margin weakly convex. Pronotum saddle-shaped, wider than long, the anterior lobe rather short with a very weak median notch; posterior margin nearly straight, also with a very weak median notch; lateral margins a single smooth curve; posterolateral corners broadly rounded; margins and disc with a few erect hairs. Legs short, hairy, tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Abdomen elongate, densely hairy. Measurements (holotype, mm): head length (to mandible base) 1.23; head width 0.92; head height 0.61; head index (width/length) 0.75; labrum length 0.19, width 0.26; left mandible length 0.80; head-mandible length index (left mandible length/head length) 0.65; postmentum median length 0.70; maximum postmentum width 0.34; postmentum waist width 0.27; pronotum length 0.34, width 0.57; pronotum/head width index 0.62; pronotum length/width index 0.60; antenna 13-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: head, labrum, postclypeus and pronotum pale yellow to yellowish brown; antennae yellowish brown, distinctly paler at the base; abdomen yellowish white; legs nearly white with a tinge of yellow. Head, thorax and abdomen moderately hairy. Body length (excluding antennae) 4.65—4.76 mm. Head nearly square, the lateral margins slightly expanding anteriorly, the posterior margin rounded; fontanelle indistinct; eyes and ocelli absent; antenna 13-segmented, segment 3 about half as long as segment 2 or segment 4 and the shortest, the segments enlarging from segment 5 on, the last segment oval and the longest. Postclypeus raised, with a distinct median longitudinal line, hairy; anteclypeus a narrow white band, its anterior margin projecting forward in the middle, hairless. Labrum dome-shaped, distinctly wider than long, the lateral margins convex, the anterior margin nearly straight, with several long and short hairs. Left mandible with 1 apical and 2 marginal teeth at the apex, the apical tooth finger-like, the first marginal tooth narrower, slightly longer and close to the apical tooth, the second marginal tooth small and situated far below the first marginal tooth; the right mandible likewise with 1 apical and 2 marginal teeth, the apical tooth nearly triangular and sharp, the first marginal tooth triangular and slightly smaller than the apical tooth, the second marginal tooth smaller, blunt and adjacent to the first marginal tooth; molar plate well developed, with oblique fine ridges. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, much wider than long, the anterior lobe rounded without a median notch, the posterior margin nearly straight without a median depression, the lateral margins expanding anteriorly, the anterolateral corners narrowly rounded. Legs hairy, tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Abdomen elongate, hairy; cerci 2-segmented, without styli. Minor worker similar to the major worker but slightly smaller. Measurements (mm, 10 individuals): major worker head length (to mandible base) 0.86—0.91, head width 0.91—0.96, head height 0.46—0.53, labrum length 0.29, labrum width 0.34—0.38, pronotum length 0.24, width 0.58—0.60; minor worker head length 0.68—0.72, head width 0.76—0.81, head height 0.43—0.48, labrum length 0.20—0.24, labrum width 0.34, pronotum length 0.22—0.24, width 0.48—0.53.

note: Adapted from species No. 22, "Microcerotermes biswanathae sp. nov.", in Maiti & Chakraborty (1994) "Termite fauna (Isoptera) of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Indian Ocean" (Records of the Zoological Survey of India, Occasional Paper No. 167), original in English; the alate is recorded in the original as "Unknown", and only the soldier and the major and minor workers are described. The item-by-item comparisons with the related species (M. heimi, M. tenuignathus, M. insularis, M. minutus, M. minor), the type specimens and type locality, the distribution and the illustrations in the original have not been entered.
